title: The Web’s Core: Request to Render

scenes.line2: you hit Enter on a URL?
scenes.say: Ever wonder what actually happens when you press Enter on a web address? Let’s break down the journey, step by step.

scenes.label: DNS
scenes.sub: Browser finds the server’s IP address.
scenes.say: First, your browser uses DNS to turn the domain name into an IP address, so it knows where to send your request.
Next, it connects using TCP or QUIC. If it’s HTTPS, TLS encrypts everything. Then, the browser sends an HTTP request.

scenes.title: Server replies
scenes.say: The server responds with HTML and maybe other resources. Your browser starts building the page.
Caching helps speed things up by reusing resources. CORS controls which sites can fetch data, protecting your app.

scenes.question: Does the browser store session data?
scenes.right: No, session data is usually on the server. The browser stores only a session ID, often in a cookie.
scenes.say: Careful: The browser doesn’t store your session data—just a session ID, usually in a cookie. The real data lives on the server.
